p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** Seven lessons from turning a discipline into a distributable package: what a package *is*, what ships inside it, what establishes its identity, how it builds without polluting the consumer, and when to generalise its machinery.

p.each-lesson-is-self-contained: Each lesson is self-contained — the failure that taught it, the law in one bolded line, the mechanics, and a "symptoms you need this" line.

p.vocabulary-is-generic: Vocabulary is generic — *the package*, *the consumer*, *the slot* — because the laws port even where the build system does not.

package-is-project.title: P1 — a package is a project

p.p1-context-a-bespoke-layout-costs-an-aut: **Context.** If a package has its own bespoke layout, an author must learn a package-only directory convention, and the tooling that validates an ordinary project cannot be pointed at a package.

p.p1-context-two-shapes-means-two-of-every: Two shapes means two of everything — two linters, two mental models, two ways to be wrong.

p.P1-LAW-A-PACKAGE-IS-A-PROJECT: **The law.** *A package is a project — the distributable unit is structurally identical to a working project, with no package-only convention to learn.*

p.P1-MECHANICS-SPEC-SUBTREE-CODE-AT-THE-RO: **Mechanics.** Prompt and spec content lives under a `spec/` subtree laid out exactly as an ordinary project's; arbitrary code lives at the root (a build manifest plus source), exactly as a project root holds it; one manifest file names the package.

p.P1-MECHANICS-AUTHORING-A-PACKAGE-IS-AUTH: Then authoring a package *is* authoring a project — the same check command applies unchanged, the same boot computation runs, the same layout is validated by the same rules.

p.P1-MECHANICS-CODE-IS-OPTIONAL: Code is optional: a prompt-only package simply has no code at its root.

p.P1-MECHANICS-ONE-OBJECT-MADE-INSTALLABLE: The distributable and the working project are one object, one made installable.

p.p1-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** A package-only folder convention nobody remembers; a project linter that refuses to run against a package; documentation that exists only to explain how packages differ from projects.

ship-runtime.title: P2 — ship the runtime, not a description of it

p.p2-context-the-tooling-was-hardcoded-ins: **Context.** The discipline's tooling was hardcoded inside one workspace.

p.p2-context-installing-gave-a-description: Installing the discipline package gave a consumer a *description* of checkers they did not have — to actually run the discipline they would have to re-implement the very tools already written.

p.p2-context-documented-but-not-distributa: The practice was documented but not distributable.

p.P2-LAW-SHIP-THE-RUNTIME-NOT-A-DESCRIPTIO: **The law.** *Ship the runtime, not a description of it — a practice's tooling travels inside the package.*

p.P2-MECHANICS-THE-PACKAGE-CARRIES-THE-EXE: **Mechanics.** If a package documents a checker, a linter, a generator, or a build step, the package carries the **executable** form of it, not only the prose.

p.P2-MECHANICS-THE-EXACT-FAILURE-TO-DESIGN: "Install X and you get a description of a tool you do not have" is the exact failure to design out.

p.P2-MECHANICS-THE-ARTIFACTS-AND-THE-RUNTI: A consumer who installs the package holds the working tool the same moment they hold the words that describe it — the strong-author artifacts (the guide, the cards) and the runtime (the checkers) ship together or the practice is not really distributable.

p.p2-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** "Install this, then go build the tool it describes"; a practice only its author can actually run; a gap between what the doc promises and what the install delivers.

identity-is-source.title: P3 — identity is the source, excluded by denylist

p.p3-context-hashing-the-whole-directory-p: **Context.** Hashing or copying a package's whole directory pulls in build output — non-deterministic (timestamps, host paths, incremental state) and potentially gigabytes.

p.p3-context-that-makes-identity-unstable-: That makes identity unstable and materialisation ruinous: the same source yields a different hash on every build, and the copy drags tens of GB of artifacts.

p.P3-LAW-IDENTITY-IS-THE-SOURCE-EXCLUDED-B: **The law.** *Identity is the source, never build artifacts — exclude them by a denylist of never-source directories, not a per-file allow-list.*

p.P3-MECHANICS-A-SHORT-DENYLIST-NAMES-WHAT: **Mechanics.** A short denylist names what was **never** source — VCS internals, caches, build output (for example `.git/`, `target/`, `node_modules/`) plus an optional package-level ignore file.

p.P3-MECHANICS-HASH-COPY-AND-SLOT-OPERATE-: The identity hash, the snapshot copy, and the materialised slot all operate over the source *minus* that denylist.

p.P3-MECHANICS-IT-MUST-BE-A-DENYLIST-NOT-A: It must be a **denylist, not an allow-list**: a per-file allow-list resurrects a write manifest that someone has to maintain and breaks the verbatim guarantee — a human reading the package directory should see *exactly* what materialises, with no path rewriting and no hidden selection.

p.P3-MECHANICS-THE-DENYLIST-INTRODUCES-NO-: The denylist only formalises "what was never source"; it introduces no choice.

p.p3-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** Identity changes when nothing but the build changed; a per-file ship list nobody keeps current; a materialise step that copies gigabytes of build output.

build-output-elsewhere.title: P4 — build output goes to a gitignored location

p.p4-context-building-consumer-side-in-pla: **Context.** Once a package can carry code, building it consumer-side is tempting to do in place.

p.p4-context-in-tree-output-pollutes-and-f: But writing build output into the committed tree pollutes it, and folding that output into identity (P3) makes the hash flip on every build.

p.P4-LAW-BUILD-OUTPUT-GOES-TO-A-GITIGNORED: **The law.** *Build output goes to a gitignored location, never the committed tree and never the identity hash.*

p.P4-MECHANICS-THE-HOOK-DIRECTS-OUTPUT-OUT: **Mechanics.** A build hook directs its output to a gitignored path **outside** the committed slot; the hook is handed the project root so it can address that location explicitly.

p.P4-MECHANICS-THE-SLOTS-RESET-SEMANTICS-A: The slot's reset semantics are then trivially safe — there is nothing in the slot to reset, because the build never wrote there.

p.P4-MECHANICS-A-LANGUAGE-NATIVE-CONSUMER-: A language-native consumer may instead reference the shipped source through its own toolchain and skip the hook entirely.

p.P4-MECHANICS-THE-TREE-AND-THE-HASH-SEE-O: Either path, the committed tree and the identity hash see only source; build output lives where version control already ignores it.

vendor-bootstrap.title: P5 — vendor and commit the bootstrap toolchain

p.p5-context-a-chicken-and-egg-risk: **Context.** A tool that consumes its own discipline toolchain has a chicken-and-egg risk: a fresh clone cannot build because the tool that builds it is not there yet.

p.p5-context-the-bootstrap-must-exist-befo: The bootstrap has to come from somewhere that exists before the first build.

p.P5-LAW-VENDOR-AND-COMMIT-THE-BOOTSTRAP-T: **The law.** *Vendor and commit the bootstrap toolchain beside the code that needs it — there is no chicken-and-egg.*

p.P5-MECHANICS-THE-CONSUMED-TOOLCHAIN-LIVE: **Mechanics.** The consumed toolchain lives in a **committed** slot, so a fresh clone builds from a clean checkout with **no prior install step** — the dependency target already exists in the tree.

p.P5-MECHANICS-THE-DEVELOPMENT-LOOP-STAYS-: The development loop stays ergonomic: editing the in-repo package source re-materialises the slot on the next install, so the consumed copy tracks the edited source without a manual wipe.

p.P5-MECHANICS-VENDORED-VERSIONED-AND-OFFL: The toolchain a build needs is vendored beside the code that needs it, versioned and offline- buildable — not fetched from a network the first build cannot yet reach.

p.p5-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** "Run the installer before you can build the installer"; a clone that will not build offline; a bootstrap step that assumes the tool is already on the search path.

spike-first.title: P6 — spike before the irreversible move

p.p6-context-a-cross-workspace-topology-ha: **Context.** Relocating code across a workspace boundary, or adopting a cross-workspace topology, has sharp platform-specific edges — on one OS, path canonicalisation adds a prefix and the build tool mishandles it.

p.p6-context-discovering-it-after-the-move: Discover that *after* the move and you have paid for a migration you must now unwind under pressure.

p.P6-LAW-SPIKE-THE-RISKY-TOPOLOGY-BEFORE-T: **The law.** *Spike the risky topology empirically on the target platform before the irreversible move; keep an evidence-chosen fallback.*

p.P6-MECHANICS-VALIDATE-ON-THE-ACTUAL-TARG: **Mechanics.** Before physically relocating anything, validate the risky arrangement on the **actual target host** — the one with the sharp edges, not the friendliest one to hand.

p.P6-MECHANICS-CHOOSE-THE-FALLBACK-ON-SPIK: Keep a rejected-but- retained alternative ready, and choose between the primary design and the fallback on spike **evidence**, not by default or by taste.

p.P6-MECHANICS-THE-MOVE-HAPPENS-ONLY-AFTER: The irreversible move happens only after the topology is proven to work where it actually has to.

p.p6-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** A migration that works on the author's OS and breaks on the user's; a topology adopted on faith and unwound in a panic; "it should work" standing in for "I ran it on the target."

build-on-demand.title: P7 — build the general mechanism on real demand

p.p7-context-a-neutral-core-is-tempting-to: **Context.** A language-neutral core is a genuine reusable artifact, and that makes it tempting to extract up front.

p.p7-context-extracting-before-a-second-co: But extracting it before a second consumer exists is speculative: you design the abstraction against a single use, and the second use reshapes it anyway — so you pay for generality twice.

p.P7-LAW-EXTRACT-WHEN-THE-SECOND-CONSUMER-: **The law.** *Extract the general mechanism when the second consumer arrives, not before.*

p.P7-MECHANICS-SHIP-IN-ONE-PLACE-AND-DOCUM: **Mechanics.** Ship the whole thing in the one place that needs it now, and **document** the future extraction as a clean follow-up with an explicit trigger ("taken when the first non-X pilot needs it").

p.P7-MECHANICS-THE-ORDERING-IS-DRIVEN-BY-R: The end state may well be symmetric — a neutral core with per-language frontends — but the ordering is driven by real second-consumer demand, not built on speculation.

p.P7-MECHANICS-EXTRACT-AGAINST-TWO-REAL-US: When the second consumer is real, you extract against **two** real uses instead of one imagined one, and the abstraction fits on the first try.

p.p7-symptoms: **Symptoms you need this.** An abstraction with exactly one caller; a "reusable core" reshaped the moment its second user appears; generality paid for long before it earns out.

item.SUM-P1-A-PACKAGE-IS-A-PROJECT: P1 — a package is a project; the same layout, the same checks, no package-only convention.

item.SUM-P2-SHIP-THE-RUNTIME: P2 — ship the runtime, not prose describing a tool the consumer never receives.

item.SUM-P3-IDENTITY-IS-THE-SOURCE: P3 — identity is the source, excluded by a denylist of never-source dirs, never a per-file allow-list.

item.SUM-P4-BUILD-OUTPUT-GOES-ELSEWHERE: P4 — build output goes to a gitignored location, outside the committed tree and the hash.

item.SUM-P5-VENDOR-THE-BOOTSTRAP: P5 — vendor and commit the bootstrap toolchain beside the code that needs it.

item.SUM-P6-SPIKE-FIRST: P6 — spike the risky topology on the target platform first; keep an evidence-chosen fallback.

item.SUM-P7-BUILD-ON-REAL-DEMAND: P7 — extract the general mechanism when the second consumer arrives, not on speculation.
